subject: [PATCH v6 RESEND 1/5] mm/memcontrol: flatten try_charge_memcg control flow

2026-09-28.patch_summary: This patch refactors the try_charge_memcg function in the Linux kernel's memory control module to simplify its control flow by separating the logic for memsw and memory page counters into distinct paths.

reviews.author: Harry Yoo
reviews.summary: Approved the patch and gave it a Reviewed-by tag. Found no issues with the refactoring.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 12:23:44PM -0700, Joshua Hahn wrote:
> Refactor try_charge_memcg by flattening the nested memsw/memory
> page_counter operations to separate the logic between the two.
> 
> When page_counter_try_charge is made stock-aware, this flattening makes
> the control flow easier to follow since each page counter now has its
> own success/failure paths.
> 
> No functional changes intended.
> 
> Acked-by: Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev>
> Signed-off-by: Joshua Hahn <joshua.hahnjy@gmail.com>
> ---

Looks good to me,
Reviewed-by: Harry Yoo (Meta) <harry@kernel.org>

-- 
Cheers,
Harry / Hyeonggon

2026-09-29.patch_summary: The patch refactors the try_charge_memcg function in mm/memcontrol.c to simplify its control flow by separating page counter operations for memsw and memory. This change is intended to make the code easier to follow when page_counter_try_charge becomes stock-aware.
